vote.summary: The canonical design contract fully specifies the NSG-as-shared-policy model, typed Subnet/NIC badges, focused Security view, interaction contract, validation states, accessibility, migration/rollback, failure paths, option ledger, and acceptance checks. All acceptance criteria are met, material alternatives are assessed, and retained implementation unknowns are explicitly scoped out and do not block approval.
requirements_covered: Azure NSG is represented as one shared policy resource in a policy library/inspector with association count
Each valid application is surfaced as a compact typed badge on the associated Subnet or NIC
NSG peer cards, generic ports, and NSG-to-VM connections are removed from the default canvas
Association lines and overlays appear only in the focused Security view
Add/attach flows support drag plus picker equivalents, valid-target-only highlighting, Attach NSG mode, and required named-NIC chooser for collapsed/multi-NIC VMs
Select/inspect flows distinguish the shared NSG, the exact association badge, and target Security layers with provenance
Edit, detach, reuse, and delete flows include blast radius, shared-resource confirmation, detach-only semantics, and target enumeration before deletion
Unattached, incomplete, invalid, multiple-layer, effective-concern, and unknown/provider-unverified states are explicitly represented
Migration and rollback preserve provider truth and legacy metadata without guessing NICs or mutating cloud resources
Accessibility, keyboard, color-vision, and screen-reader equivalents cover every status, relationship, and action
Option ledger A-F and all acceptance checks are satisfied by the selected hybrid model
implementation_options: A - improved peer node (rejected; migration-only reversible legacy view)
B - target badge on Subnet/NIC (selected default in-canvas representation)
C - security boundary/overlay (retained only as on-demand Subnet visualization)
D - association edge (retained only in focused Security view, dashed, non-arrowed, labelled)
E - separate policy library (retained as single home for identity, unattached resources, and lifecycle)
F - hybrid progressive disclosure (selected: B+E primary, C+D controlled inspection aids, A migration-only)
details_checked: Badge is a view of an association, not a copy of the NSG; VM summary expands to named NICs and never attaches the badge to VM identity
Security view uses dashed, non-arrowed, labelled 'applies to' lines without topology ports and hides them when focus/layer mode ends
Collapsed/multi-NIC VM attach requires a named-NIC chooser; no silent primary NIC selection
Delete of an attached/reused NSG lists every known target and offers Cancel, Replace where supported, or Detach all and delete
Unattached NSG stays editable in Policies with informational Unattached state; no floating topology node
Migration preserves IDs, names, rules, provider metadata, and legacy layout/link metadata; converts only proven NSG-to-Subnet/NIC edges; unresolved imported targets remain non-healthy migration items
Rollback restores the prior representation from preserved metadata without changing provider resources
Validation state uses icon/text/accessible name, not color alone, and identifies whether uncertainty belongs to policy, association, target, or effective result
Provider verification unavailability preserves intended edits as pending/unverified and never fabricates effective rules
Low zoom collapses badges to shield plus count/status without removing all evidence that policy is applied
vote.proposed_artifact: No replacement needed; the canonical design contract v0 is accepted unchanged.
